target.title: refactor: extract chat abort handling from gateway handler
target.body:
Closes #106085

## What Problem This Solves

`src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` remained a high-churn god file with roughly 1,300 lines of abort authorization, run cancellation, worker coordination, and transcript persistence mixed into the other chat RPC handlers. That broad review surface made abort changes harder to reason about and kept the LOC ceiling unnecessarily high.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extracts the complete `chat.abort` subsystem into focused authorization, handler/runtime, text-normalization, and transcript-persistence modules while preserving the existing RPC, shared-state, and cancellation contracts. The handler table now delegates `chat.abort`, and the LOC ratchet for `chat.ts` drops from 5,336 to 4,002 lines; every new module stays below 500 lines.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Maintainers get smaller ownership boundaries, isolated testable helpers, less conflict pressure in `chat.ts`, and a lower enforced ceiling that prevents the subsystem from drifting back into the god file.

## Evidence

- `CI=1 OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed` — passed on exact head in Testbox `tbx_01kxd0qk30gk8fb7dc28v4dhnv` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29227536749)).
- `CI=1 corepack pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-authorization.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-persistence.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts` — 5 files / 257 tests passed on exact head in the same Testbox run.
- `CI=1 corepack pnpm test:gateway` — 442 files / 7,281 tests passed before the conflict-free rebase ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29226915721)).
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` — clean twice; final review confidence 0.98.
- `node scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- AI-assisted; implementation and extracted control flow reviewed in full. No changelog entry because this is an internal behavior-preserving refactor.
